title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 47
summary: Personally inspect 36 roots: 31 additions, one fork consolidation and four qualified deferrals.
notes: Root personally ran 48 cross-platform searches yielding 516 hits and 514 repository roots, inspected 36selected roots and prepared 31additions with 5non-promotions. No discovery worker used. Platforms searched span classic computers, handhelds and consoles; no claim every platform is exhausted. Snapshot baseline 9f3d1f3cff1c80cf2c4e46d724c4cc3016eccca8 has 4222projects. No upstream program, ROM, installer, firmware or emulator executed. Ingestion findings: forks require lineage review; generated machine-register C warrants BAKED EMULATION architecture tagging rather than an unqualified native-port claim; an API reimplementation alone is not baked emulation. README platform labels can conflict with compile-time target macros. Byte-exact DEFB payloads do not prove symbolic instruction recovery; INCLUDE_ASM C files do not prove decompiled bodies. Unsupported README API routes failed visibly and were replaced with supported pinned tree/file reads. Empty content from an oversized source file was not counted as inspected source: a smaller source representation was read instead. Mixed read/write benchmarks and bounded behavioral examples must keep their limits. Retired tool bundles should preserve successor relationships. No arbitrary current completeness percentage or independent build claim was inferred.

sources.reason: Paper-listing recovery and original 48K snapshot preservation alongside 128K remakes. Original game lacks the final Kamuir level; context explicitly parks endgame work. The inspected dark1 main source still emits substantial code as DEFB bytes, so byte-perfect is not equivalent to fully symbolic instruction recovery.

PC-98 disk-image and executable analysis toolkit with Rust image modules and Python Capstone 16-bit x86 decoder. README decompilation and porting goals are not proof of a complete automatic port pipeline. V30 extension coverage is not independently validated.
Character-table and shifted-symbol decoding research. Source implements bytes-to-text but text-to-bytes is a pass stub; this is not a completed translation patch.
Translation repository with a C script extractor, fixed ROM table offsets and Japanese symbol mappings. Do not infer a complete playable translation from the repository name.
Matching game C and separate SDK-based host client. Inspected C defines recovered game/media structures; original PsyQ libraries are linked separately, not counted as newly decompiled game logic.

Matching and reconstruction tracks coexist. Inspected aiinit.c is INCLUDE_ASM wrappers, not recovered C bodies; README percentages are dated author reports, not a current semantic completeness measure.
In-progress US-release decompilation with build/extract scripts. Inspected player.c retains INCLUDE_ASM bodies. README explicitly says code is not yet shiftable.
In-progress reconstruction with named actor/game state structures, overlay handling and asset extraction tools. Primary support is US1.1; other versions only minor support.
US ROM reconstruction; inspected entry C creates native libultra threads. Setup generates assembly for nonmatched functions, so buildability does not establish complete C recovery.

Browser-local IPS/BPS patch engine and WonderSwan translation catalogue. Inspected parser handles patch headers, buffer growth and bounds. CERTIFIED and PRACTICAL are project-defined verification labels, not independent tracker certification.

Assembler-buildable cartridge and QUEST/PENNIES reconstruction plus bounded Python behavioral examples. GPL is interpreted game code; do not mislabel this as native TMS9900 instruction reconstruction. Source sample provides mapped variables and structured GPL representation.
Julius1.8.0 port maintained as patches and RISC OS packaging. Inspected patch implements desktop logging, filename treatment, platform sources and frame yielding.

Reads native font descriptor/content files, exports JSON and converts to TTF/OTF/UFO. Inspected big-endian FontStreamer decodes bitmap rows and pointers. Host-side font work, not an Amiga execution CPU requirement.
Native bootblock and launcher source by Ross preserved by earok. Closes CLI/Workbench and reclaims Chip RAM for floppy-launched programs. Inspected assembly uses Exec/DOS/Intuition services.
Preserved GadToolsBoxv3 source for native GUI/resource creation and C code generation. Inspected C generator includes native Amiga APIs and emits windows, gadgets and locale assets.

Standard/extended DSK inspection, MGT/SAM handling, BASIC/screen viewers and copy-protection identification. Inspected Pascal packed records implement disk and track structures; media CPU is not a host CPU constraint.

Historical CPC cross-development container and examples. Dockerfile installs build tools and cpclib. README explicitly recommends rust.cpclib instead; retain as a historical bundle, not the current recommended workflow.

GAC sample adventure reimplemented in C on a BBC Master and refactored on A5000. Inspected extensionless C/gCode contains gameplay/counter/inventory interface. Do not infer6502 execution from BBC branding when Norcroft C environment is unspecified.
Terry Kyriacopoulos DOS3.3 image utilities maintained by Cats Eye, with explicit ANSI-C Unix/MS-DOS portability changes. Historical fork attribution preserved; one tool suite record.

Python CF-image partition inspection/extraction/assembly for MicroDrive/Turbo. Inspected source embeds6502 boot bytes; that is image content, not Python host CPU. Distinguishes HFS detection from assumed ProDOS on other partitions.
Go resource-fork parser with big-endian resource-map decoding and typed resource extraction. Not a native68k application merely because inputs are Macintosh files.

Standalone standard-C++ resource abstractions and Mac/Palm format classes. Explicitly work in progress; sample map implementation initializes fields and must not be treated as proof all resource operations are finished.
Native Z80 diagnostics for display modes, sprites, keyboard, joystick and PSG. Inspected source selects ROM/COM/CAS/BASIC output formats and BIOS calls.

Native CPU-frequency and mixed read/write memory benchmarks with opcode-based CPU detection. Inspected SDCC naked Z280 probe; Z280 detection marked experimental. Timing is VDP-interrupt-based and approximate, not a universal CPU-clock oracle.
PNG-to-Screen2 sprites, tiles and SCR converters used for Night Knight. Supports16x16 sprite decomposition and256tile limit; output C/assembly is data, not a CPU-bound program.
Native IPv4 UDP SNTP client for ESP/X libnetwork sockets and Human68k RTC setting. C implementation avoids floating point and64-bit assumptions; README documents legacy socket-API quirks.
Native DaynaPORT network-adapter driver tooling for BlueSCSIV2 on X68000; inspected SCSI C implementation. Separate from BlueSCSI firmware and hardware.
Partial sound-bank disassembly and compression/tile research. Dynamic-programming RLE encoder and in-budget reskin scripts are implemented; not a full game-source reconstruction.
On-machine assembler/editor/linker with instruction timing analysis. Inspected opcode cycle tables support the documented Z80 assembler rather than merely example binaries.
Ruby macro-assembler DSL with labels, relocation/debug metadata, TAP output and Spectrum BASIC helpers. Ruby host requirements separate from generated Z80 code.
Annotated historical assembler/editor/monitor reconstruction with installer and relocation/configuration tables. Inspected source documents interleaved code/data and relocation design.
GitHub identifies this as a fork of blondie7575/ChoplifterReverse; inspected README retains Quinn Dunki attribution and the same ProDOS-loader scope. No distinct project scope established.

BAKED EMULATION architecture audit: generated C retains6809 registers, condition codes, memory access and cycle accounting atop board-chip models, with a separate interpreter twin. The original-source-derived assembly reconstruction is genuine, but must be separated from that runtime before promotion under the existing scope policy.

BAKED EMULATION: generated C retains68000 registers, condition flags, memory-mapped STE hardware and dynamic resume dispatch. No interpreter is not equivalent to recovered high-level native game logic. Hold for architecture/scope audit.

Platform/provenance conflict: README calls this cancelled3DO UMK3 source, but inspected SYSTEM.H defines SONY_PSX and background C describes Mortal KombatIII Sony paths. Source archive exists; do not promote a3DO port without resolving identity and lineage.

Empty root README and inspected Rails model/controller provide repository CRUD scaffolding. A working Macintosh resource parser or useful recovery workflow was not established; retain a lead rather than advertise an implemented format tool.
